title: Radio transmitter (FM stereo + RDS, NFM, AM, SSB, I/Q, CW, digital, pictures, AES67)
summary: A radio station on one pin, made inside the FPGA: FM stereo with your station name and text on the radio's display (RDS), NFM, AM, USB, LSB, DSB and I/Q, Morse code, RTTY, PSK31 to PSK250, QRSS, Hellschreiber and WSPR, pictures in an SDR's waterfall, SSTV and radiofax pictures, APRS packets, DTMF, songs from WAV files and live sound from the network (AES67).
wiring: a short wire, 10 to 20 cm, as the antenna
a few meters of range in a room; the self-test needs nothing
J9 pin 11 through a 1 kohm resistor
an SDR input (RTL-SDR) through a 30 to 40 dB attenuator
never the pin straight into an SDR: the resistor and the attenuator protect it and keep the signal off the air
the ground (outer conductor) of the SDR cable
parts: an FM radio with RDS (a car radio, a kitchen radio, a phone with an FM chip)
optional: an RTL-SDR stick to see the spectrum, the RDS, the digital modes and pictures painted into its waterfall
tested: the self-test passed 41 of 41 checks on the real board (November 2026, with the I/Q mode), with nothing connected; the new modes 21 of 21 on the board (radio_gen_test.py) and 42 of 42 on the PC (radio_modes_test.py).
